draft.title: What adaptations improve
card: Chronic adaptations change what the body can do in performance. Several measures improve together.

VO2 max, the highest rate of oxygen use, rises. The lactate inflection point, the intensity where lactate starts to build up fast, moves to a higher intensity. An athlete can then work harder before tiring.
Muscle contractions become faster and stronger, which helps with speed and power.
Lactate tolerance improves. The athlete can keep going at a high intensity even with more lactate in the muscles and blood.
draft.remember: Adaptations let an athlete work harder, for longer, with more speed, force and tolerance of lactate.

a.q: After training, an athlete's lactate inflection point moves to a higher intensity. What does this allow?
opts: Harder work before lactate builds up fast
Lower VO2 max at every intensity
Slower muscle contractions at high effort
Lactate to stop forming during exercise
a.why: A later inflection point means the athlete can work at a higher intensity before lactate rises quickly. It does not stop lactate forming, which is the tempting wrong option.
a.clue: The point has moved to a higher intensity.

b.q: Jo, a Ballarat 800 m runner, trains for a season. Which result shows improved lactate tolerance, not a higher inflection point?
opts: She holds her pace in the last 200 m despite high lactate
She runs at a faster pace before lactate starts to build
Her oxygen use at maximum effort goes up
Her muscles contract with more force
b.why: Lactate tolerance is keeping going at high intensity while lactate is already high. Running faster before lactate builds describes a higher inflection point, which is the tempting wrong option.
b.clue: Tolerance is about coping once lactate is already high.

a.best: Harder work before lactate builds up fast

b.best: She holds her pace in the last 200 m despite high lactate

problems.detail: The three wrong options are all plain reversals or impossibilities (lower VO2 max, slower contractions, lactate stopping). A Year 12 student can rule them out without understanding the lactate inflection point.

The distractor 'Lower VO2 max at every intensity' muddles the concept. VO2 max is a single maximal value, not something measured at every intensity, so the option could confuse students about what VO2 max is.

check.summary: The facts match the VCE study design, and both questions have one clear right answer. Question a is too easy, because its distractors are obvious reversals, and one distractor misuses the term VO2 max.

a.q: After training, an athlete's lactate inflection point rises. What does this change allow?
opts: Working harder before lactate starts to build up fast
Keeping going once lactate in the blood is already high
Using oxygen at a higher rate at maximum effort
Making muscle contractions faster and more forceful
a.why: A higher inflection point means the athlete reaches a higher intensity before lactate rises quickly. Keeping going once lactate is already high is lactate tolerance, a separate improvement and the tempting wrong option.
a.clue: Think about when lactate starts to build up fast.

b.q: Jo, a Ballarat 800 m runner, trains for a season. Which result shows improved lactate tolerance, not a higher inflection point?
opts: She holds her pace in the last 200 m despite high lactate
She runs at a faster pace before lactate starts to build
Her oxygen use at maximum effort rises over the season
Her leg muscles contract with more force in her sprint
b.why: Lactate tolerance is keeping going at high intensity while lactate is already high. Running faster before lactate builds describes a higher inflection point, which is the tempting wrong option.
b.clue: Tolerance is about coping once lactate is already high.
